subject: DONE s321: s/// replacement now interpolates like a dq string — FOUR silent-wrongs closed
description:
SHIPPED b3be060.

_gen_interp_replacement was a hand-rolled mini-interpolator (knew \1..\9, $1..$9, ${name}, $name with name starting [a-zA-Z_]); everything else fell through as LITERAL TEXT. It now routes through the real double-quoted-string parser (CLAUDE.md 11 — `"$h{$1}"` was already correct), with \1..\9 normalised to $1..$9 first since that is the one rule a replacement has and a dq string does not. The old function survives as _gen_interp_replacement_simple for the single shape PPI cannot take (a trailing odd backslash would eat the closing quote).

FOUR classes fixed, not one:
  1. subscripts    s/(a)/$h{$1}/  -> "{a}"    (the reported bug)
  2. arrays        s/a/@arr/      -> "@arr"   (no @ branch existed)
  3. ${digit}      s/(a)/${1}x/   -> "${1}x"  (brace branch required a letter)
  4. punctuation   s/a/$^O/       -> "$^O"    (bare-name branch required a letter)
3 and 4 were LIVE in the shipped corpus — perl-tests/sprintf.t emitted both as literal text, which is how corpus-diff found them.

VERIFIED: corpus-diff 3 of 111, all explained (ref.t + reset.t = benign single-var shape change, a bare atom becoming a one-element p-string-concat; sprintf.t = the two real fixes). Gate 125 files / 4470 PASS. Sweep 0 new / 0 fixed vs 689. Cache generation v2-91 -> v2-92.

GUARD: Pl/t/transpile-test-09.t — 14 replacement forms in one 3 s snippet, covering the four fixed classes AND every form the old path handled (both backref spellings, dq escapes, escaped $, braced NAME, literal backslash, /e).

NOTE for whoever measures perf: the single-variable replacement now costs one p-string-concat call it did not before. Unwrapping a one-element concat would restore the old shape, but the old shape returned a BOX where the concat returns a STRING, so it needs a deliberate check that p-subst treats them identically — not worth doing blind.
